title: Recap: *-va/-ve* states, and verbs of lying and standing

sections.title: What you know
sections.content: You know the participle in *-va/-ve* from B1 Unit 29 and the state with *van* + *-va/-ve* from B2. This lesson uses the participle to describe damaged land: it names the state, and a verb such as *fekszik* ('lies') or *áll* ('stands') says where the land or the thing is.

sections.title: Example
sections.content: *A talaj kiszáradva fekszik a nyári napon.* ('The soil lies dried out in the summer sun.') The participle stays the same for singular and plural: *A mocsarak lecsapolva fekszenek.*

sections.title: Patterns in Context
rows: A talaj kiszáradva fekszik a nyári napon.
The soil lies dried out in the summer sun.
A folyó betonfalak közé szorítva folyik a városon át.
The river flows squeezed between concrete walls through the town.
A mocsarak lecsapolva, a rétek felszántva fekszenek az egykori ártéren.
The marshes drained, the meadows ploughed, lie on the former floodplain.
